messages.subject: Plot with Double Scale
parts:
Dear All,
First of all I would like to thank everyone for their help on this list.
I am migrating some R codes of mine from base graphics to ggplot2.
Does anyone know how to generate a plot with two different scales in
order two plot two (wildly) different functions of the same variable in
the same figure?
To fix the ideas, consider the following snippet where 'conc' and 'temp'
are a concentration and a temperature


x <- 1:10
temp <- rnorm(10, mean=5-20*x)
conc <- rnorm(10, mean=x)

b <- diff(range(temp))/diff(range(conc))
a <- min(temp) - b*min(conc)

par(mar=c(5,5,5,5))

plot(x, temp, ylim = range(c(temp, a + b*conc)), type='l')
lines(x, a + b*conc, lty=2)

ticks <- pretty(conc)
axis(4, at=a + b*ticks, labels=ticks)
mtext("conc", 4, 3)
legend("top", c("temp", "conc"), lty=1:2)


Does anybody know how to achieve the same using ggplot2?
Cheers

Lorenzo

messages.subject: Re: Plot with Double Scale
parts:
See here http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/b48984c4f660eb5a.

Using two different vertical scales on the same plot is a bad idea.

Hadley
